issues.legal_issue: A statutory bar on appeals from orders in summary possession proceedings does not exclude an appeal under a High Court charter from an order made by a single judge exercising original jurisdiction unless the statute expressly excludes charter appeals.
material_facts: The suit was brought under a statutory procedure for recovery of possession, and a single judge of the High Court exercising original jurisdiction decreed it.
An appeal was filed before a division bench under the High Court’s charter.
The respondents argued that the statutory provision barring appeals and revisions made the appeal unmaintainable.
The statutory bar did not expressly exclude appeals under the High Court’s charter.
issues.conclusion: The charter appeal was maintainable, and the matter was restored to the High Court for the appeal to proceed.
issues.legal_principle: The statutory provision barring an appeal or revision from an order under the summary possession procedure bars an appeal under that provision, but does not cut across the High Court’s constitutional power or exclude an appeal available under its charter unless the statute expressly does so. Under clause 15 of the Letters Patent, an appeal lay from a judgment of a single judge exercising original jurisdiction. The Court relied on section 6(3) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 and clause 15 of the Letters Patent; it cited no earlier cases.

rule.if: summary_possession_case and single_judge_original_order and charter_provides_appeal and statutory_bar_not_expressly_covering_charter_appeal

predicates.summary_possession_case: The proceeding was brought under a summary procedure for recovery of possession.
predicates.single_judge_original_order: A single judge made the challenged order while exercising the court’s original jurisdiction.
predicates.charter_provides_appeal: The court’s charter provides an appeal from a judgment of a single judge.
predicates.statutory_bar_not_expressly_covering_cha: The statutory restriction on appeals does not expressly exclude appeals available under the court’s charter.

issues.definition: When a summary possession proceeding produces an original-jurisdiction order by a single judge, the charter provides an appeal, and the statutory restriction does not expressly cover that charter appeal, the charter appeal is maintainable.
